seoTitle: How to Create a Calendar View in Airtable
metaDescription: Build an Airtable Calendar view by mapping a date field, dragging cards to reschedule, and sharing a live link, plus which calendar features are paid-plan only.
intro: A grid full of start dates and deadlines is useful, but it doesn't show your schedule the way a calendar does, bunched by week with gaps and overlaps obvious at a glance. Airtable's Calendar view reads the date fields you already have and lays every record onto a month grid you can drag records around on to reschedule them. This guide covers making sure your table has a usable date field, adding a Calendar view, mapping it, and what changes if you need a date range instead of a single day.

steps.heading: Open the base from your Airtable home screen
steps.body: From Home you'll see recently opened bases listed by name, workspace, and when they were last touched. Open the base with the table you want to turn into a calendar. A content calendar or project tracker is the obvious fit, since those tables almost always already have date columns you can reuse.

image.caption: Airtable's Home screen, listing recently opened bases. Pick the one with the table you want to visualize as a calendar.

steps.heading: Confirm your table has a usable date field
steps.body: Before creating the Calendar view, check your grid for a date column, something like Start date or Deadline. If none exists, add one the way you'd add any column: the plus icon at the end of the header row, then the Date field type. Rows with no value in the field you eventually choose won't show up on the calendar until you fill one in. Check for blanks now, before the view exists; it's easier to fix here than after.

image.caption: A grid table with Start date, Deadline, Assignee, and Status columns already in place — everything the Calendar view needs to map from.

steps.heading: Create the Calendar view
steps.body: In the Views sidebar, click Create new and choose Calendar from the list of view types. Name it for what it tracks, like Editorial Calendar or Launch Timeline, and pick whether it's collaborative (visible and editable by anyone with base access) or personal (visible only to you). You can add more Calendar views later, mapped to different fields or filtered to a subset of records, so this first one doesn't need to be perfect.

steps.heading: Map a date field to the calendar
steps.body: A "Choose date fields" dialog asks which field decides where each record sits on the grid; pick your primary date, such as Deadline, and every account can do this on any plan. Two things above that are gated to paid plans. Setting a second, end-date field so a record spans several days as a bar instead of showing as a single-day dot needs a Team plan or higher, and so does mapping more than one date field onto the same calendar. On Airtable's Free and Plus plans, a Calendar view maps to one date field, one day per record.

image.caption: The Choose date fields dialog, where you tell the Calendar view which date column to plot records against — Deadline, in this case.

steps.heading: Reschedule by dragging cards
steps.body: Once mapped, every record with a date lands on its day, and anything missing a date shows up in the sidebar under a "without dates" list so nothing gets lost. Drag a card from the sidebar onto a day to give it a date, or drag a card already on the calendar to a different day to reschedule it. Either action updates the date field in the underlying table immediately, not just the card's visual position.

steps.heading: Color-code and share the calendar
steps.body: Use the Color button in the toolbar to color records by a field like Status or Assignee, which speeds up scanning a busy month for what's overdue. When it's ready to hand off, use Share and sync to generate a link; you choose whether it's view-only or editable, so outside collaborators can see the schedule without necessarily being able to change it.

costNote: Calendar views themselves are free on every Airtable plan, including Free. What costs money is the multi-day version: mapping a start date and an end date so a record shows as a bar, and mapping more than one date field to the same calendar, both require a Team plan or above. A single date field, one day per record, works on any plan.

troubleshooting.problem: A record never shows up on the calendar
troubleshooting.cause: The field mapped to the view is empty for that record.
troubleshooting.fix: Drag the record in from the "without dates" sidebar list, or fill the date field directly in the grid.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no option to add an end date or a second date field
troubleshooting.cause: Date ranges and multiple mapped date fields are limited to Team-plan and above; Free and Plus only support a single date field per Calendar view.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade the workspace, or track start and end as two separate single-date Calendar views on a lower plan.

troubleshooting.problem: A teammate doesn't see the reschedule you just made
troubleshooting.cause: The view was created as Personal, not Collaborative, so only you can see changes to it.
troubleshooting.fix: Recreate the view as collaborative, or change its visibility from the view's settings menu.

faq.question: Does dragging a card on the calendar update the underlying data, or just the display?
faq.answer: Yes. Moving a card in the Calendar view updates the corresponding date field in the base's underlying table immediately.

faq.question: Can I have multiple calendar views for the same table?
faq.answer: Yes, you can create several Calendar views mapped to different date fields or filtered to different subsets of records.

faq.question: Is a date range (start and end date) a free feature?
faq.answer: No. Showing a record as a multi-day bar, by mapping both a start and an end date field, requires a Team plan or higher. Free and Plus accounts map one date field per calendar.

faq.question: Is the shared calendar link editable by outside viewers?
faq.answer: That depends on the sharing permissions set when the link is generated; it can be configured as view-only or editable.

faq.question: What happens to a record with no date filled in?
faq.answer: It appears in a separate "without dates" list in the sidebar instead of on the grid, until it's dragged onto a day or the date field is filled in manually.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough of the Calendar view. Re-checked against Airtable's own help center in September 2026, which surfaced a plan gate the article didn't previously mention: date ranges and multiple mapped date fields need a Team plan or higher, not just any paid plan, and the Free plan supports only a single date field per Calendar view. That constraint is now reflected in the mapping step, costNote, troubleshooting, and FAQ.
